title: Notable recent Mathematics papers on arXiv — 16 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is an inferred editorial selection of notable recent papers, not a popularity ranking; comparative citation and independent-attention evidence is too sparse for newly announced work. The authors' claims are preprint claims, not independently checked proofs.

sections.title: Region bounds, error margins and certified positivity in the numerical conformal bootstrap; Or the first mathematically rigorous bounds on the 3d Ising CFT critical exponents
sections.abstract: The author closes four gaps between numerical conformal-bootstrap bounds and theorems—parameter-region coverage, unbounded spin, true rather than truncated conformal blocks, and floating-point rounding—and applies exact certificates to bound 3d Ising critical exponents under stated spectrum assumptions.
sections.claimed_result: The author certifies that for Δσ∈[0.505,0.5405], Δε∈(1/2,3] is excluded except for a small rectangle containing the 3d Ising island, yielding two-sided bounds on η and ν under explicit spectrum assumptions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Numerical conformal bootstrap for the 3d Ising CFT; the flagship bounds depend on explicitly stated spectrum assumptions. Certification uses exact arithmetic, Bernstein-basis positivity certificates, and control of the infinite-spin tail and true conformal blocks.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is conditional on the assumed spectrum and is not a proof of the full CFT construction. The paper says the mixed-correlator extension still has a finite list of certificates to run.

sections.title: The Bardos-Tartar Conjecture for the Navier-Stokes Equations
sections.abstract: The authors prove the Bardos–Tartar density conjecture for two-dimensional periodic Navier–Stokes with time-independent forcing, extend it to a hyperviscous family, and establish additional backward-extendability results in dimensions two and three.
sections.claimed_result: For 2D periodic Navier–Stokes, the authors prove that data whose solutions extend backwards to any fixed positive time are dense in the mean-zero divergence-free L² space; they also prove the analogous density result for their hyperviscous equations.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Incompressible viscous equations on the periodic domain, positive viscosity, time-independent forcing; the density theorem is in dimension two. Separate backward-extendability statements cover dimensions two and three.
sections.unique_caveat: The conjecture-resolution claim is two-dimensional; the additional 3D results do not establish global regularity or a 3D version of the density theorem.

sections.title: A quantitative form of the planar Falconer distance theorem
sections.abstract: The authors give a quantitative planar distance-set lower bound under Frostman growth assumptions, recovering positive Lebesgue measure for compact planar sets of Hausdorff dimension above one.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that a compact planar set of Hausdorff dimension greater than one has a distance set of positive Lebesgue measure, with a uniform positive lower bound under normalized Frostman assumptions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Compact planar sets; the normalized theorem assumes support in the unit ball and a probability measure satisfying ν(B(x,r)) ≤ 2r^(1+η), for 0<η<1.
sections.unique_caveat: The quantitative estimate is not claimed sharp and gives neither the endpoint power nor a pinned-distance conclusion; the authors describe the approach as a planar development of an earlier multiscale manuscript.

sections.title: Imaginary quadratic fields of class number at most 2000
sections.abstract: The paper reports an unconditional classification of imaginary quadratic fields with class number at most 2000, including 16,453,493 fields and Lean-checked zero-free-region and discriminant-bound arguments.
sections.claimed_result: The author reports exactly 16,453,493 fields, with largest absolute discriminant 1,062,350,083; the zero-gap and resulting large-discriminant bounds are formalized in Lean and reported checked by two kernels.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Imaginary quadratic fields with class number at most 2000; the computation combines a zero-free-region bound, class-group tables for smaller discriminants, and a sieve for the remaining range.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper states that the sieve program itself is not formally verified and that some low-discriminant class-number data come from prior tables. The recent zero-free-region manuscript it builds on is explicitly described as not refereed.

sections.title: The asymptotic Erdős–Frankl–Füredi cover-free conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors prove the Erdős–Frankl–Füredi asymptotic threshold for when an r-cover-free family can have more members than points, establishing T(r) ≥ r²+r+2 for every r≥1.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove T(r) ≥ r²+r+2 for all r≥1, which together with the known asymptotic construction yields T(r)=(1+o(1))r².
sections.assumptions_and_setting: T(r) is the least ground-set size for which an r-cover-free family has more sets than points; no member is contained in the union of at most r other members.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem establishes the asymptotic threshold, not an exact value of T(r) for every r; the matching upper bound is supplied asymptotically by the known affine-plane construction.

sections.title: A Proof of the Area Vanishing Square Peg Conjecture
sections.abstract: The author resolves a problem posed by Tao related to the Toeplitz square-peg conjecture, proving that four once-winding polygonal curves in a cylinder jointly inscribe a square when an alternating area condition vanishes.
sections.claimed_result: Four simple closed polygonal curves in the cylinder, each winding once positively, jointly inscribe a square if the alternating sum of their ∫y dx integrals is zero.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Four simple closed polygonal curves in a cylinder, each with winding number one in the positive direction, satisfying the specified alternating integral constraint.
sections.unique_caveat: The result proves the area-vanishing case related to the Toeplitz square-peg problem, not the full square-peg conjecture for arbitrary curves.

sections.title: A counterexample to the generalized Viterbo conjecture on the spectral distance in a disc cotangent bundle
sections.abstract: The authors prove unboundedness of spectral distance for Lagrangians Hamiltonian-isotopic to the zero section under topological assumptions on a closed manifold, disproving a generalized Viterbo conjecture; they also classify surfaces where the conjecture holds over Z₂.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that spectral distance is unbounded on the stated space of Lagrangians for closed manifolds satisfying specified topological assumptions; they classify all surfaces for which the conjecture holds over Z₂.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Lagrangians Hamiltonian-isotopic to the zero section in a disc cotangent bundle of a closed manifold, with the theorem's topological assumptions; the surface classification uses coefficients Z₂.
sections.unique_caveat: The counterexample applies under the stated topological assumptions; the result does not say the conjecture fails for every closed manifold or every coefficient system.

sections.title: A New Bound for the Gauss Circle Problem
sections.abstract: The authors improve the uniform error term in the planar Gauss circle problem to E(X)=Oε(X^(209/670+ε)) for every ε>0.
sections.claimed_result: For real X≥4, the authors prove E(X)=Oε(X^(209/670+ε)) for every ε>0.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: E(X) is the lattice-point count in the radius-√X disk minus its area πX; the estimate is uniform for real X≥4.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper presents an exponent improvement, not an optimal error term; no sharpness claim is made in the abstract.

sections.title: The monodromy conjecture for high order poles, and norms of residue antiderivatives
sections.abstract: The author proves a strong local monodromy statement for poles of order at least n−1 of the naive motivic zeta function of a complex polynomial in n variables and constructs associated homology eigencycles.
sections.claimed_result: The author states that each covered pole has a local homology exp(2πis)-eigencycle near a contributing one-dimensional exceptional stratum; the proof combines topological methods with a birational-geometric fact described as AI-discovered.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A complex polynomial in n variables and poles of order at least n−1 of its naive motivic zeta function; the construction is local near a contributing one-dimensional exceptional stratum.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated result covers only the specified high-order poles; it should not be read as resolving the conjecture for every pole. This is a new preprint, not an independently reviewed result.
